home.trust_title: It designs everything. Only what you approve counts.
home.trust_lead: In machine control, what matters is not who wrote the first version but who stands behind it. That is why {{site.brand}} does as much of the design work as possible and lets nothing through without a decision by the responsible person.

trust.name: You approve items, not the whole project
trust.desc: Every device, the I/O table, sequence, interlocks, limits, simulation result, every safety function, the safety program and the commissioning plan separately. With name, date and note.

trust.name: Approval is tied to content
trust.desc: A fingerprint of what you approved is stored. Change a step time, an address or a PLr and the item goes back for approval. Editing a description or switching language does not cancel the approval.

trust.name: Unapproved items are visible
trust.desc: Documents with unapproved items carry a prominent NOT APPROVED. The safety program is only generated once the safety functions have been approved.

trust.name: The documentation shows who approved what and when
trust.desc: The approval record is part of the machine documentation: status of each item, name, date, note and content fingerprint. For the customer, for the technical file and for later changes.

home.trust_note: Proposals come with reasoning and sources: the ISO 13849-1 risk graph and tables, catalogue values of components, simulation results. {{site.brand}} plans the validation of safety functions on the machine according to ISO 13849-2 and prepares the record for it. A person carries it out and signs it.
home.docs_title: Documentation you can hand to your customer
home.docs_lead: One machine description produces the complete set, and it stays consistent. Add a valve and it appears in the I/O list, terminal plan, schematic, FDS, alarms, FAT and bill of materials at once.
home.local_body: Both the desktop application and the web version run on your computer. We do not store projects on any server. If you work under an NDA with a carmaker or an OEM, there is nothing to explain.
home.local_ai: The exception are the AI features: proposing a device list from a free-text description and reading schematics and photos of an existing machine. When you use them, the text or image is sent to the AI provider. Without them nothing leaves your computer. The application only goes online to activate the licence and occasionally to check it, without any project content.

faq.a: Propose, yes. Decide, no. {{site.brand}} prepares a proposal with reasoning and sources, but until the responsible person approves it, it is not valid anywhere and no safety program is generated. Responsibility stays where it always was. You just have a record of what you checked.

{{site.brand}} builds documentation, schematics, program and calculations by fixed rules: the same input always gives the same output. AI only helps where the input is free-form: it proposes a device list from a machine description and reads signals from schematics or photos of an existing machine. That too is a proposal you review and approve.

faq.q: Is the program ready to load into the PLC?
faq.a: It is a complete program with state machines, modes, faults and acknowledgement, and the design is verified by simulation. We verified import and compilation in real CODESYS V3.5 SP21 without errors or warnings; Schneider, WAGO and Delta AX have the language verified, not the devices and addresses. The other platforms are checked by our emulator, which is not the manufacturer's compiler, so they are marked beta. We have not verified download to a PLC on any platform. Before commissioning, the program belongs in your platform's simulator and on the FAT.

faq.q: I have an existing machine. Do I have to re-enter it?
faq.a: No. {{site.brand}} reads an export or program from the PLC (TIA Portal, Studio 5000, ST sources, tag tables) and derives devices, I/O, sequence and interlocks from it. For every item it shows where it came from and how certain it is.

faq.q: What if a real job exceeds the {{site.free_io_limit}} I/O limit?
faq.a: Write to us and we will unlock your first project above the limit completely free. Further machines of that size need the Pro plan.
Yes. Only the AI features need the internet. The licence is a signed file that the application verifies offline.

home.end_title: Try it on a machine you know
home.end_body: Take a smaller machine you know by heart. In an afternoon you will see whether the outputs suit you.

platformy.title: Platforms and verification — {{site.brand}}
platformy.description: Siemens, Rockwell, Beckhoff, CODESYS, Schneider, WAGO, Delta Electronics, Mitsubishi, OMRON and Unitronics. What is verified by import in the IDE, what by the compiler and what by the emulator.
platformy.h1: 10 platforms. We say what is verified.
platformy.lead: We verified CODESYS by real import and compilation in CODESYS V3.5 SP21 Patch 6: examples in classic and OOP style, drives and the servo axis without a single error or warning. Schneider, WAGO and Delta AX use the same CODESYS language; for them we verified the language and the import, not the libraries, devices and addresses. The other platforms are checked by our emulator. We have not yet tried the import in the manufacturer's development environment, so they carry a beta label.

rows.name: Siemens SIMATIC
rows.output: SCL sources, SimaticML XML, tag table
rows.check: emulator: SCL parser and dialect rules from Siemens manuals, run against the machine model; SimaticML format

rows.name: Rockwell Allen-Bradley
rows.output: L5X (Add-On Instructions, tags, routine) and tag CSV
rows.check: emulator: L5X and Logix dialect per manual 1756-RM014, run against the machine model; real L5X exports

rows.name: Beckhoff
rows.check: emulator: ST parser for TwinCAT, run against the machine model; PLCopen TC6 schema

rows.name: CODESYS
rows.check: PLCopen XML import and compile in CODESYS V3.5 SP21 Patch 6 (3.5.21.60), 5 October 2026: classic and OOP, drives and SoftMotion servo axis, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Run on the runtime (download to the PLC) not verified

rows.name: Schneider Electric
rows.check: language and PLCopen import: CODESYS 3.5.21.60 compiler; Schneider libraries, devices and I/O addresses not verified

rows.name: WAGO
rows.output: PLCopen XML, ST blocks, GVL (I/O mapped in the IDE)
rows.check: language and PLCopen import: CODESYS 3.5.21.60 compiler; WAGO libraries, devices and I/O addresses not verified, SoftMotion Light servo axis not verified

rows.name: Delta Electronics AX
rows.check: language and PLCopen import: CODESYS 3.5.21.60 compiler; Delta libraries, devices and I/O addresses not verified

rows.name: Mitsubishi

rows.name: OMRON

rows.name: Unitronics
rows.check: emulator: flat ST from Unitronics manuals, run against the machine model; the dialect will be confirmed by the first compile

legend.text: We imported and compiled the output in the manufacturer's real development environment. The How it is verified column gives the version and date. Download to the PLC and running on the runtime are not verified by this.
The platform is built on CODESYS V3.5. The language and the PLCopen XML import passed the CODESYS compiler; we have not verified the manufacturer's libraries, devices and I/O addresses in its IDE.

The code passed our emulator: our own parser and dialect rules from the manufacturer's manuals, and a scan-by-scan run of the program against the machine model, with no difference from the design on any example. We have not yet tried the import in the manufacturer's IDE.

platformy.why_body: The emulator is not the manufacturer's compiler. It catches what it knows from the manuals, but what the compiler of your IDE version says is confirmed only by a real import. The README for each platform therefore describes the shortest test: import, compile and run in the platform simulator. If you find a deviation, write to us. We fix it and move the platform towards verified.
platformy.safety_lead: Built from the manufacturer's certified blocks, only after the safety functions have been approved. We have not yet verified the safety program in the manufacturer's IDE, so it is beta on all platforms.

podminky.title: Terms of sale and licence — {{site.brand}}
podminky.description: Terms of sale and licence for the {{site.brand}} application: plans, subscription, licence, nature of outputs and limitation of liability.
podminky.lead: These terms govern the use of the {{site.brand}} application (desktop application and web version) and the related website services. The application is intended primarily for businesses: integrators, machine builders and designers. Article 9 additionally applies to consumers.

sections.h: Operator and conclusion of the contract
body: The operator is {{site.operator.name}}, company ID {{site.operator.id}}, registered office {{site.operator.address}}, e-mail {{site.email}} (the “operator”).

The licence agreement is concluded by downloading the application with consent to these terms (Free plan) or by completing an order for a paid plan (Pro, Company). The contract is concluded in Czech or in the language selected on the website.
The operator grants the user a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the application within the scope of the selected plan, for the term of the contract and without territorial restriction.
- Free: free of charge and without time limit, projects up to {{site.free_io_limit}} I/O, exports with the {{site.brand}} footer, no DXF export.
- Pro: no project size limit, exports without footer, DXF export; one computer.
- Company: the scope of Pro for a team, up to 5 computers, own library of block templates.
The number of computers is controlled by licence activation. The operator releases a licence from another computer on request.
The user may not resell the licence or provide it to third parties, circumvent licence mechanisms or reverse engineer the application, except where permitted by law.
Outputs the user creates in the application (documentation, schematics, program) belong to the user. The footer in Free plan outputs must not be removed.
Paid plans are paid monthly in advance according to the price list on the website. Prices are shown excluding VAT; consumers see the final price including VAT before completing the order.

Payments are processed by Stripe or Paddle. When paying via Paddle, Paddle is the seller (Merchant of Record) and its terms also apply to the purchase itself; Paddle issues the receipt and remits VAT.

The subscription renews automatically for another month until cancelled by the user. It can be cancelled at any time, effective at the end of the paid period. Payment for a started period is not refunded unless the law provides otherwise.

If a payment fails, the licence remains functional for at least one month after the end of the paid period. After cancellation or persistent non-payment the application switches to the Free plan; the user's data and projects remain on the user's computer.
The operator will announce a price change at least 30 days in advance by e-mail. The new price applies from the following period; the user may cancel the subscription before the change.

sections.h: Nature of the outputs: the application proposes, a responsible person decides
body: The application proposes machine control: devices, I/O, schematics, process logic and PLC program, safety functions including PLr, architecture, components and a program for the safety PLC, a commissioning plan and documentation. All outputs are a proposal for review.

Only items approved by the user's responsible person (name, date, note) are valid. Approval is an act of the user, not of the operator. Unapproved outputs are marked NOT APPROVED and must not be used as a basis for manufacturing, wiring or putting the machine into service.

The simulation in the application verifies the design, not the program compiled in the PLC manufacturer's development environment. Outputs for the individual platforms have not been verified by compiling in the manufacturer's development environment, with the exception stated on the Platforms page.
Outputs of the AI features (device list proposal, reading of schematics and photos) may be incorrect or incomplete; the application always presents them as a proposal for review.

sections.h: Responsibility of the machine manufacturer and integrator
body: The machine manufacturer, or the integrator who designs the control system and puts it into service, is responsible for the machine, its control and safety. In particular, they are responsible for the risk assessment, the design and validation of safety functions according to ISO 13849-1 and ISO 13849-2 (or IEC 62061), compliance with Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the technical file, the EU declaration of conformity and the CE marking.

The application is not a certified tool for developing safety systems and does not replace professional competence, risk assessment, verification of the program on the target platform, FAT or validation on the machine. The application plans the validation of safety functions and helps record it; a person carries it out and signs it.
The application is provided as is. The operator is not liable for its suitability for a particular purpose of the user unless expressly promised.

To the extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for indirect damage, loss of profit, loss of data, downtime, or damage caused by using outputs that the responsible person has not verified or approved, or by using them contrary to articles 4 and 5.

The operator's total liability to the user under the contract is limited to the amount the user paid to the operator in the 12 months before the damage occurred. For the Free plan, for which the user pays nothing, the operator is liable only to the extent that cannot be excluded by contract.

These limitations do not apply to harm to life, health and other natural rights of a person, to damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence (Section 2898 of the Czech Civil Code), or to consumer rights that cannot be limited by contract.

The AI features are optional. When used, the application sends the entered text, documents or images to the AI provider (Anthropic) using the user's API key. The user is responsible for the provider's terms and costs of use; the operator has no access to the data sent.

The user is responsible for being allowed to pass the documents to the AI provider (for example with regard to confidentiality towards their customers). Without these features, project content stays on the user's computer.

The application works without an internet connection. Website services (download, licence activation and check) may be temporarily unavailable; the licence is therefore verified offline with a grace period.

Support is provided by e-mail without a guaranteed response time unless agreed otherwise. Updates may change application features; the operator will announce any substantial restriction of paid features in advance.

A consumer may withdraw from a distance contract without giving a reason within 14 days of its conclusion by e-mail to {{site.email}}. The operator will refund payments received within 14 days of withdrawal.

For digital content not supplied on a tangible medium, the right of withdrawal ends when performance begins if the consumer gave prior express consent and acknowledged losing the right of withdrawal (Section 1837(l) of the Czech Civil Code). This consent is given when ordering.
The consumer has rights arising from defective performance of digital content and services under the Civil Code; defects can be reported by e-mail.
The contract is governed by the law of the Czech Republic, in particular the Civil Code. The UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

Disputes with businesses are decided by the general courts of the Czech Republic competent according to the operator's registered office. This does not deprive consumers of the protection afforded by mandatory provisions of the law of their country of residence.

Consumers may resolve disputes out of court with the Czech Trade Inspection Authority (www.coi.cz, ADR department). The European online dispute resolution (ODR) platform ceased operation on 20 July 2025.

soukromi.title: Privacy policy — {{site.brand}}
soukromi.description: What personal data {{site.brand}} processes, why, for how long and what rights you have.
soukromi.lead: We process only what we need to deliver the application, licences and payments. We do not process the content of your projects: it stays on your computer.

body: The controller of personal data is {{site.operator.name}}, company ID {{site.operator.id}}, {{site.operator.address}}. Data protection contact: {{site.email}}.

sections.h: What data, why and on what basis
body: - Download form: e-mail, language, visit source (utm), time of consent to the terms and time of download. Purpose: to provide the download link and record consent to the licence terms. Basis: performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

- Licence: e-mail, licence key, plan, anonymous computer fingerprint, the computer description you enter, times of activation and checks. Purpose: issuing the licence and controlling the number of computers. Basis: performance of a contract.

- Payments: from the payment service we receive the e-mail, subscription identifier and payment status; payment details (card) never reach us. Purpose: issuing and managing the licence, accounting. Basis: performance of a contract and legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)).
- Communication: the content of e-mails you send us. Purpose: replies and support. Basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).

- Website protection: IP address and technical browser data during Turnstile verification and in the hosting's operational logs. Purpose: protecting forms against bots and service security. Basis: legitimate interest.

- Customer admin: only the operator has access to the data above, through the protected customer admin (sign-in with a token, or via Cloudflare Access), and may add a note to a customer for support and licence management. Every view of a customer's details, every action (issuing, extending or cancelling a licence, releasing a computer, adding a note) and every export is written to an audit log (who, when, what). Failed sign-in attempts are recorded with the IP address and browser details to protect against misuse. Purpose: licence management and data security. Basis: performance of contract and legitimate interest.

- Business contacts (B2B): in an internal record of sales opportunities we keep companies that might use {{site.brand}} — for companies from our own research only publicly available company data (name, website, segment, city, country, link to the source); the contact person's name, phone and e-mail are added manually only once we are in contact with the company. It also includes download-form leads (e-mail and status: download, trial, licence) only to see the stage of the relationship (we do not use this data for marketing). Purpose: managing business relationships and offering the product to companies. Basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)). You can object to this processing at any time at {{site.email}} — we will then delete the record and not create it again. We do not send commercial e-mails without your consent unless you are our customer.
We do not use your data for marketing, do not send newsletters without your express consent and do not carry out profiling.
Projects (machine descriptions, I/O, schematics, programs, documentation) are processed by the application only on your computer; they are not uploaded to our servers.

The exception are the optional AI features: when used, the application sends the entered text, documents or images directly to the AI provider (Anthropic, PBC, USA) using your API key. This processing is governed by the agreement between you and the provider; we have no access to the data sent. You do not have to use the AI features.
- Cloudflare, Inc.: website hosting, database, Turnstile protection. Transfer to the USA based on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses.

- Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. (Ireland), or Paddle.com Market Ltd. (United Kingdom) as seller (Merchant of Record) and independent controller of payment data; the service used depends on the selected payment method.
- Resend (Plus Five Five, Inc., USA): sending e-mails with the link and licence, once enabled.
- GitHub, Inc.: hosting of download files; processes your IP address when downloading.
We do not sell data or pass it on to other parties unless required by law.
- Download form data: 3 years after the last download, then deleted.
- Licence data: for the duration of the licence and 3 years after it ends.
- Accounting and tax documents: 10 years under Czech VAT and accounting law.
- Hosting operational logs: according to the provider's settings, usually days to weeks.
- Customer admin: audit log 3 years, failed sign-in attempts 30 days, customer notes for as long as the customer's data is kept.
- Business contacts: for as long as sales talks continue, at most 3 years after the last contact; immediately after an objection.

You have the right of access to your data, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and portability, the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest and to withdraw consent where processing is based on consent. Just write to {{site.email}}; we will reply within a month.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (www.uoou.gov.cz) or the supervisory authority of your country.
This policy applies from {{site.legal_effective}}. We will inform you of substantial changes on the website and, if you hold a licence, by e-mail.

cookies.title: Cookies — {{site.brand}}
cookies.description: The {{site.brand}} website uses no analytics or advertising cookies.
cookies.lead: The website uses no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies and stores nothing in visitors' browser storage. That is why we do not ask for consent with a banner. The only exception is a strictly necessary cookie for the operator's sign-in to the customer admin (see Administration); it does not concern website visitors.

body: - Fonts are system fonts; the website loads no external libraries or fonts.
- The Download page loads Cloudflare Turnstile protection. It processes technical browser data to tell humans from bots; it sets no advertising or analytics cookies.
- Cloudflare hosting may set a strictly necessary technical cookie for security reasons (for example __cf_bm). It serves only to protect the service and expires after 30 minutes at most.
- If visitor statistics are enabled, we will use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies.
When ordering a paid plan, the payment window of Stripe or Paddle opens. It may set its own necessary cookies according to its policies, for example for payment security and fraud prevention.
The /admin/ page is for content administrators only. When signing in via GitHub, it stores sign-in data in the administrator's browser storage.

The customer admin page (/sprava/) is for the operator only. After sign-in it sets a single strictly necessary cookie, __Host-plcdesk_admin: it contains only a signed random session identifier and its expiry, lasts at most 8 hours and is deleted on sign-out. It is sent only over HTTPS, only to this website, and is not accessible to page scripts. It is never set for website visitors. The admin also remembers the chosen language in the operator's browser storage.
If the operator signs in via Cloudflare Access, Cloudflare sets its own strictly necessary sign-in cookie (CF_Authorization) under its own policy.
You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings. The website will keep working; without Turnstile protection the download form may refuse to submit.
This information applies from {{site.legal_effective}}.
